solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poetry, say, on the verge of being included in correspondence

indicators.note: being included in tells us one piece sits inside the word for correspondence

parts.note: a fit is a correspondence or match between two things
on the verge of something is near to it

explanation.surface: A poet on the brink of being quoted in someone's letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poetry, say' marks the definition as an example: poetry is one of the arts in that category.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry is one example of the creative disciplines grouped together as the arts valued for beauty.

clue.text: The French military cover fake pickle jars

indicators.note: jars, as containers, hold the answer inside the run of letters of fake pickle

explanation.surface: French soldiers concealing fake pickle in jars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jars' reads as a noun after 'pickle', but it is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is the flat-topped peaked cap worn by French soldiers and police.

clue.text: Woman with rupees deposited in it

indicators.note: deposited in tells us the pieces are placed inside the word for it

parts.note: it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA
with means and, in addition

explanation.surface: A woman banking her rupees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' as sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra is a female given name, so any woman could be clued this way.

clue.text: Revolutionary's southern location for filming All the King's Men?

parts.note: Che Guevara is the revolutionary, plus the possessive S
a set is where a film is shot

explanation.surface: A revolutionary picking a southern setting to shoot a film of the political novel All the King's Men.
explanation.walkthrough: All the King's Men is a novel and film title; here it means the pieces on a chessboard, the king's side and all.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxed collection of chess pieces holds every man belonging to each king on the board.

clue.text: Sweet to catch big game in Zone One — ecstasy!

indicators.note: in places the hunting phrase inside the letters for zone, one and ecstasy

parts.note: A means one
E is the drug ecstasy
to bag game is to catch it
a lion is the classic big game animal

explanation.surface: A hunter's thrill at bagging a lion in the first sector.
explanation.definitionFit: Zabaglione is an Italian dessert of whipped egg yolks, sugar and Marsala wine.

clue.text: Force to underwrite endorsement's opposite number

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing under means coming after the other piece

parts.note: a visa is an endorsement in a passport
vis is Latin for force

explanation.surface: Applying pressure to get someone to guarantee a counterpart's endorsement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to underwrite' looks financial, but in a down answer it places VIS below VISA.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterpart who faces one directly is one's vis-a-vis, the person opposite.

clue.text: Enjoy eating bananas with great speed

parts.note: to enjoy something is to like it
bananas is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone who loves eating bananas wolfing them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like food but is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes doing something furiously fast, as in running flat out.

clue.text: The man sporting top that is item from car boot sale?

indicators.note: sporting means wearing, so the cap is worn around the man

parts.note: a cap is a top for the head
the man is he
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A man in a cap selling junk at a car boot sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A car boot sale is a British flea market where people sell junk from the backs of their cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods at such markets are typically low-priced, so a bargain item is aptly a cheap thing.

clue.text: Go north and wait in pub (The Old Penny — average)

indicators.note: in places the reversed verb and the waiting word inside the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: going north in a down clue means reading upwards

parts.note: to stand is to wait
D (denarius) was the old British penny before decimalisation

explanation.surface: Heading up to the pub to wait, at a bar called The Old Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north' turns GO upwards to OG. The old penny (pre-1971 British coin) was written d.
explanation.definitionFit: A British colloquialism for something entirely ordinary, plain and unremarkable.

clue.text: Dutch duke aboard rickety Iron Horse

indicators.note: aboard puts the duke's letter on board, inside the jumbled letters
rickety means shaky, so the letters are unsteady and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Dutch duke riding a creaky old railway engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is Cockney for wife (my old Dutch, from duchess), not a nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British humorous terms for a man's wife, the stay-at-home partner of comedy.

clue.text: A pint of beer not quite finished by Greek hero

indicators.note: not quite finished drops the last letter of the drink

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a pint of beer
X is the times sign, as in four by two

explanation.surface: A Greek hero not quite downing his pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was a hero of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Unlawful entry gained by inserting spring into lock

indicators.note: inserting puts the spring word into the word for lock

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A burglar getting in by forcing a spring into a door lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' and 'spring' look like locksmith's parts; they are hair and a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Going onto property without permission is the tort of illegal intrusion.

clue.text: Ploughman's lunch, say, a group consumed in grass

indicators.note: consumed in means eaten up inside the word for grass

parts.note: to grass is to inform, to squeal
R.E.M. is an American rock group

explanation.surface: A group eating a ploughman's lunch sitting on the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is the British slang verb to inform, not the lawn. A ploughman's lunch is a British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A filling, substantial meal; the ploughman's is given as one example.

clue.text: Woman said rocky bed's way to succeed

indicators.note: to succeed is to come after, so the route follows
said tells us the word is spoken, keeping only its sound

parts.note: a sill is a sheet of rock lying between beds of other rock
via means by way of

explanation.surface: A woman described as finding her way to success on a bed of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: A sill in geology is a flat intrusion of igneous rock between strata.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvia is a female given name, so any woman could be clued this way.

clue.text: What's instinctive when out getting catering order

indicators.note: order as a verb asks for the letters to be put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: Instinctively going out to get a catering order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a noun after 'catering', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An immediate response felt without thinking is a reaction from the stomach, an instinctive one.

clue.text: Unpleasant patches encountered after wrong turning across border

indicators.note: across means the border word straddles the rearranged letters

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge

indicators.note: turning signals the letters are twisted round into a new order

explanation.surface: Nasty patches of ground met after taking a wrong turning across a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' shuffles WRONG to NGWOR, which the border RIM spans.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungal skin infection that shows as red circular patches on the skin.

clue.text: Indigenous American dog nipping stray cat

indicators.note: nipping means biting, holding the other piece in its jaws

parts.note: a chow is a breed of dog

indicators.note: stray means wandering, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A Native American's dog biting a stray cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stray' rearranges CAT to CTA, which the dog is nipping.
explanation.definitionFit: The Choctaw are a Native American people originally from the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: Reminder for 4 captured by London police ring

indicators.note: captured by puts the 4-down pieces inside the police word

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
4-down's contents are pieces, or men, on the board
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A souvenir for a gang caught by the London police.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' points to 4-down, whose contents are chessmen: MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake that makes one remember a person or event is a souvenir.

clue.text: Woman unfortunately has nothing in navy

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things go wrong, so the letters are jumbled
in puts the zero inside the navy abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A woman with nothing left in the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharon is a female given name, so any woman could be clued this way.

clue.text: Circle Line network on which young woman's travelling westbound

indicators.note: in an across answer travelling west means reading right to left

parts.note: a rete is an anatomical network of nerves or vessels
a maid is a young woman

explanation.surface: A young woman riding the London Underground's Circle Line westbound.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground line; here it means a line through a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight segment passing through a circle's centre is that shape's key line.

clue.text: Woman's three distinct articles

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the is the definite article
a is the other form of the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman with three separate items to her name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' are the grammatical ones, not items.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthea is a female given name, so any woman could be clued this way.

clue.text: Worthless individuals Leinster No. 8's ejected from melee

indicators.note: ejected from means thrown out of the melee word

parts.note: a scrum is a confused melee

indicators.note: No. 8 here asks for the eighth letter of Leinster

explanation.surface: Rugby: Leinster's number eight sent off from a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Leinster is an Irish rugby team and No. 8 a scrum position, but here it is the eighth letter of 'Leinster'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dregs of society, contemptible people, as froth skimmed off the top is waste.

clue.text: Write illegibly on unusually headed stationery — such may bug me

indicators.note: writing illegibly scrambles the letters of the word written
unusually headed means the first letter is shifted from its normal place

parts.note: paper is stationery

explanation.surface: Scribbling on oddly headed notepaper; such people may annoy me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'illegibly' jumbles WRITE to WIRET; 'unusually headed' moves PAPER's first P along, giving APPER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who eavesdrops on phone lines plants listening devices, a different sense of bug.

clue.text: Receptacle into which to wee, wee again — and stick!

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot
go is another word for urinate

explanation.surface: A potty-training instruction, ending with a command to stick at it.
explanation.definitionFit: The pogo is the spring-loaded pole one bounces on, so it is a type of stick.

clue.text: Ghastly nag gets out of taxi

indicators.note: gets out of here means the horse word goes outside the taxi word

parts.note: a mare is a horse, a nag
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A horrible horse climbing out of a cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets out of' looks like leaving; it means MARE gets outside CAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome and horrifying, dwelling on death, as in a grisly tale.

clue.text: Having importance is why I get agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone explaining why they get worked up about serious matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of great consequence is heavy or significant, using weight as a figure for importance.
